checks.text: Published agent versions are immutable; drafts are mutable; deprecation is the only post-publish transition.
Every capability an agent uses resolves through a grant tied to the human user who owns the run.
Live run/session state lives in DynamoDB; completed-run lineage and message pointers land in Postgres. No entity is authoritative in both.
Agents are never principals; every external call executes as the owning user via delegated credentials.
Tool Gateway and MCP Proxy validate a Run Token on every call; no token means no egress.
Run Tokens are renewable by the harness while the parent session is alive but never outlive their run or session.
Effective scope = intersection of org policy, user consents, and agent spec scopes. Deny-by-default.
Revoking a grant blocks gateway calls within seconds.
One sandbox per session; no shared filesystem between sessions; cross-tenant retrieval impossible.
Context assembly exposes only tools in the effective grant set to the model.
Tools marked requiresApproval pause the run pending user decision; run resumes on approve/deny.
Durable state is git branches/PRs + transcript + session manifest; sandbox overlays are always discarded.
Webhook triggers are idempotent via idempotency keys; budget checked before start.
Call pipeline order: authn run token -> policy -> rate limit -> inject user creds -> execute -> redact/normalize.
A request without a valid Run Token never reaches a tool implementation.
HTTP tool egress restricted to org-configured domain allowlist.
In-session git remotes are rewritten to the facade; raw credentials never enter the sandbox.
Two users on the same MCP server never share sessions, caches, or credentials.
Model sees only tools in allowedTools intersected with the user's granted scopes.
MCP tools are exposed as mcp__<server>__<tool> to avoid collisions.
KMS root key per environment; DEKs per user/org; ciphertexts unreadable without the owning KEK.
Scrubbing middleware prevents secrets from appearing in transcripts or logs; every secret read is access-logged.
Credentials are resolved only inside gateways at call time and never written into snapshots or sandbox env.
Rate limits enforced at user, agent, org, and tool levels.
Hard budget enforcement rejects runs; soft alerts notify at 80%.
Interactive workloads are prioritized over background via separate queues/priority classes.
Every LLM call, tool call, and MCP call in a run is traced with spans correlated by run_id.
Every authorization decision is recorded to an append-only audit log (who/what/allow-deny/why).
User A can never read user B's data, snapshots, or sessions, even within the same org.
Untrusted content in context cannot trigger egress outside allowlists.
Step/token/budget caps and the kill switch stop a runaway agent.
A stolen Run Token is bound to session+sandbox, expires in 15m, and is blocked via jti revocation.
All endpoints in 12-api.md exist with the documented methods and behave as specified; no undocumented mutating endpoints.
Unauthenticated requests are rejected with 401 on all non-health endpoints.
Snapshot cache key = H(image_digest + setup hash + repo pins + builder_version + patch level); same key reuses snapshot.
Secret-scrub scan gates every snapshot publish; snapshots encrypted per-org and scoped to owner user.
Sessions attach a fresh COW overlay; the shared snapshot is never mutated; overlays discarded at session end.
Image builds run in isolated BuildKit builders outside the execution plane, network-restricted to declared allowlists.
One session owns exactly one sandbox (microVM pod); a session contains one or more runs.
Session phases transition Provisioning -> Running -> Idle -> Committing -> Terminated per spec.
Stop hook fires on idle shutdown, max lifetime, user stop, and preemption; manifest emitted before exit.
If the model fails to commit in time, uncommitted=true plus a diff blob preserves work for resume.
Resume needs only transcript + branch/PR refs from the manifest; fresh pod forks from environmentKey snapshot.
Sessions-by-org, resumable-by-user, active-per-agent lookups work via DDB GSIs; TTL expires terminated sessions.
